chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade us from the meat of the sacrificial animals after three days, then He permitted it and said: 'Eat from the meat of the sacrificial animals after three days, and store it up.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on keeping sacrificial meat for more than three days in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the jurisprudential principle of naskh (abrogation) in the context of Eid al-Adha sacrifices, where the Prophet (peace be upon him) initially restricted meat retention to three days to ensure rapid distribution to the poor, later permitting storage for sustenance. Shia scholars, such as Al-Kulayni, utilize this narration to discuss the flexibility of ritual practices and the balance between immediate charity and long-term provision, reflecting the practical needs of the early Muslim community.
